title: American Institute of Indian Studies fellowships for research in India close on 19 November
dek: AIIS is taking applications for three fellowships that fund research trips to India: one for doctoral students, one for senior scholars and one for early-career scholars. The deadline is 19 November 2026.
body: The American Institute of Indian Studies (AIIS) has opened its 2026 fellowship competition, for the 2026-27 cycle. Applications close on 19 November 2026, according to the institute's application page.

Three fellowships are on offer this round: the Junior Research Fellowship, the AIIS NEH Senior Fellowship and the Early Career Scholar Travel Fellowship. Each has its own form and instructions. Non-US citizens may apply if they are doctoral students at a US institution (junior), affiliated with a US institution (senior), or full-time faculty at a US institution (early career). For the junior and senior fellowships, applicants need not come from an AIIS member institution.

AIIS's general fellowships page, last updated in 2024, says junior fellowships support dissertation research in India for up to 11 months, with a formal affiliation to an Indian university and supervisor. Senior fellowships are for scholars with a PhD or equivalent who specialise in South Asia, and a small number of them are funded by the National Endowment for the Humanities (NEH).

Junior and senior applicants send a form with a 350-word abstract, a 150-word fieldwork justification and a short CV, plus a project statement of up to 2,100 words, a bibliography of one to three pages, a personal statement and a financial aid statement. Junior applicants also send unofficial transcripts, and anyone reapplying with the same project may add an optional revision statement. Early-career applicants send a project summary of up to 700 words, a fieldwork justification, a research output statement and a CV of up to three pages.

Junior and senior applications are judged in two rounds, with finalists announced by mid-March and recipients by the beginning of May; early-career recipients are also announced by the beginning of May. Junior and senior fellows need an affiliation certificate from an Indian research centre, and US citizens need a research visa or, for OCI cardholders, special research permission. AIIS says it helps with these documents. The award is paid on proof of travel, and fellows have two years from selection to make the trip. AIIS says its fellowship funds are extremely limited, and asks junior and senior fellows who already hold an award above $10,000 for their research to give up the AIIS fellowship.
